notes: All 11 roster entries are the targets listed in Table 1 (T:p2-b8) and are treated by the authors as known hypervelocity stars in a sample of '11 hypervelocity stars (HVSs)' (T:p1-b4, T:p1-b10); the paper is a variability follow-up and does not newly test Galactic boundness, so the entries are follow_up rather than candidates_found. HVS5's 'ambiguous' label concerns only whether it is a SPB and does not remove it as a known HVS target (T:p3-b11, T:p3-b12). The subject-heading SDSS IDs (T:p1-b5) correspond to HVS1, HVS4, HVS5, HVS7, and HVS13 via the matching Table 2 coordinates (T:p6-b0): HVS1 = SDSS J090744.99+024506.88; HVS4 = SDSS J091301.01+305119.83; HVS5 = SDSS J091759.47+672238.35; HVS7 = SDSS J113312.12+010824.87; HVS13 = SDSS J105248.30-000133.94. HVS6, HVS8, HVS9, HVS10, HVS11, and HVS12 are supplied only with HVS identifiers in Table 1. HVS2 and HVS3 are mentioned only in background discussion (T:p1-b10, T:p6-b7) and are not observed here, so they are excluded.

HVS1: Table 2 (T:p6-b0, image I:p6-b0) gives the coordinates of HVS1, identified with SDSS J090744.99+024506.88, as RA = 9:07:44.993, DEC = 2:45:06.88. The table's DEC is given in degrees-style sexagesimal notation (02:45:06.88). The listed M_B = 19.687 is an absolute magnitude, not a distance or distance modulus, so no distance is extracted. No parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

HVS4: Table 2 reports only RA, DEC, M_B, image counts, period, amplitude, chi-squared, and F-test probability for HVS4; it does not report distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability (T:p6-b0).

HVS5: The paper reports only positions for HVS5 (Table 2); no distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probabilities are given for this star. Table 2 gives RA in sexagesimal hours (9h17m59.475s) and DEC in sexagesimal degrees; the declination is positive, consistent with the identifier SDSS J091759.47+672238.35.

HVS6: HVS6 appears only in Table 1 (T:p2-b8 / I:p2-b8), which reports 8 WIYN images and no detected variability, with no MDM follow-up. The supplied material reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS6; Table 2 (T:p6-b0 / I:p6-b0), which contains coordinates and M_B, covers only HVS1, HVS4, HVS5, HVS7, and HVS13. No eligible quantity is therefore extracted for the target star.

HVS7: Table 2 lists the HVS7 coordinates without a stated epoch or equinox; they are retained as printed. The paper reports period, amplitude, M_B, chi-squared, and F-test probability for HVS7, but these are not requested quantity identifiers; M_B is an absolute magnitude, not a distance modulus. No distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS7.

HVS8: HVS8 is listed in Table 1 (LOCATION T:p2-b8; I:p2-b8) as having 8 WIYN images and no detected variability, but the paper reports no equatorial coordinates, distance/parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS8. Table 2 (LOCATION T:p6-b0; I:p6-b0), which contains coordinates for five SPB candidates, does not include HVS8. The only additional HVS8 discussion (LOCATION T:p6-b7) states that variability was not detected and that a slowly pulsating B-star nature with P ≥ 3 days cannot be ruled out; this is not one of the requested quantities.

HVS9: The target HVS9 appears only in Table 1 (T:p2-b8, I:p2-b8), which reports 8 WIYN 3.5 m images and "Variable? = No" (no MDM follow-up). No right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS9 anywhere in the paper. Table 2, which gives RA/DEC and other data, lists only HVS1, HVS4, HVS5, HVS7, and HVS13. Therefore no eligible quantities can be extracted for HVS9.

HVS10: HVS10 is only listed in Table 1 (T:p2-b8) as having 8 WIYN images and showing no variability. The paper reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS10.

HVS11: HVS11 appears only in Table 1 (T:p2-b8), where it is listed with 7 WIYN images, no detected variability, and no MDM follow-up observations. The paper reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS11, so no eligible quantities are extracted.

HVS12: HVS12 appears only in Table 1 (T:p2-b8; I:p2-b8), which reports 7 WIYN images and “Variable? No,” with no MDM follow-up. The paper does not report any eligible quantity (position, parallax/distance, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability) for HVS12. It is not among the objects in Table 2 or the SDSS identifications listed in the subject headings.

HVS13: Table 2 (T:p6-b0) reports the HVS13 coordinates in sexagesimal notation; they are retained as printed. No eligible distance, parallax, proper-motion, radial-velocity, galactocentric-radius, Galactic-rest-frame-velocity, or bound/unbound probability values for HVS13 appear in the supplied material.
